newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu in spat with professors.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu in spat with professors.

text.p: Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday cancelled an appearance at Hebrew University in a spat with professors who said the Israeli prime minister did not deserve their respect.
"I am not willing to enter a place where I am systematically denigrated," Netanyahu told Israel Radio, explaining his decision to cancel an appearance at a university convocation in three days.

The tiff erupted when leading professors wrote a letter to the university's president saying Netanyahu was "not worthy of Hebrew University's honour" and declaring their presence at the event should not be perceived as a show of respect for him.

"This prime minister has spent the whole year trying to undermine the fundamental principals of the democratic regime and has acted systematically against free press...(and) against the rule of law," said law professor Mordechai Kremnitzer.

He cited a government corruption scandal involving Netanyahu's ill-fated appointment of an attorney-general in January and other affairs during the year since the right-wing leader formed his government.

Netanyahu has had a rocky relationship with academics and journalists viewed by some in his rightist Likud party as members of an "establishment elite" that identifies with the opposition Labour party.
University president Hanoch Gutfreund said he regretted the spat and hoped Netanyahu would reconsider.
"Those professors...do not speak on behalf of the university," Gutfreund told Israel Radio. "I have always received him (Netanyahu) with respect and have always said his visits are good for us."
